paper_title: Convolutional Neural Networks and a Transfer Learning Strategy to Classify Parkinson’s Disease from Speech in Three Different Languages

sub_questions.q: Which languages are represented by the speech recordings used in the study?
sub_questions.quote: Speech recordings of patients in three different languages are considered: Spanish, German, and Czech.

sub_questions.q: Which named speech corpus provides the Spanish dataset?
sub_questions.quote: The Spanish data consider the PC-GITA corpus [6], which contains utterances from 50 PD patients and 50 HC, Colombian Spanish native speakers.

sub_questions.q: What is the speaker composition of the Spanish dataset?
sub_questions.answer: 50 PD patients and 50 healthy control speakers, Colombian Spanish native speakers.
sub_questions.quote: which contains utterances from 50 PD patients and 50 HC, Colombian Spanish native speakers.

sub_questions.q: What is the speaker composition of the German dataset?
sub_questions.answer: 88 PD patients and 88 healthy control speakers from Germany.
sub_questions.quote: Speech recordings of 88 PD patients and 88 HC speakers from Germany are considered [18].

sub_questions.q: What is the speaker composition of the Czech dataset?
sub_questions.answer: 100 native Czech speakers, comprising 50 PD patients and 50 healthy controls.
sub_questions.quote: A total of 100 native Czech speakers (50 PD, 50 HC) were considered [19].

sub_questions.q: Were the patients in the datasets evaluated with a standard clinical Parkinson’s disease scale?
sub_questions.answer: Yes, the patients were evaluated by a neurologist expert according to MDS-UPDRS-III.
sub_questions.quote: The patients in the three datasets were evaluated by a neurologist expert according to the third section of the movement disorder society, unified Parkinson’s disease rating scale (MDS-UPDRS-III) [17].
